setup: The eigenvalues are the roots of the characteristic polynomial \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).

steps.say: For a triangular matrix \(A - \lambda I\) is triangular too, so its determinant is the product of the diagonal: \(([[a]] - \lambda)([[d]] - \lambda)\); the entry [[c]] above the diagonal never enters.
Set it to zero: \(([[a]] - \lambda)([[d]] - \lambda) = 0\) gives \(\lambda = [[a]]\) or \(\lambda = [[d]]\).

answer: So the eigenvalues are the diagonal entries, [[a]] and [[d]].
